runs.text: Laplace Intelligence Launches TeraSim
-DT
Open Source Traffic Simulation Platform to Cut Delays
An Urban Digital Twin for Traffic Simulation and Management

How would a stalled vehicle disrupt traffic across a city? What happens when a major event brings thousands of additional trips into downtown? Could a different signal timing strategy help keep traffic moving?
Cities need a way to answer these “what-if” questions—to anticipate disruptions, evaluate alternative designs, and plan effective responses before making changes on the street.
Laplace Intelligence launched
TeraSim-DT
, an urban digital twin for traffic simulation that allows users to test scenarios, understand impacts across roadways, and help cities make better planning and operational decisions.
We are releasing TeraSim
-DT
as open source, making this foundation available to cities, researchers, and developers.

By turning camera observations into simulation-ready inputs and returning optimized recommendations in minutes rather than the hours or days of manual analysis, TeraSim-DT helps cities test ideas before committing field resources, and gives developers a ready foundation in place of months of building simulation workflows from scratch.
From Observation to Simulation
Intersection cameras capture how traffic moves throughout the day. TeraSim
-DT
turns those observations into inputs for simulation.

(VSS), the TeraSim platform plugs into existing workflows for detecting and tracking vehicles using camera feeds. The platform converts those observations into traffic demand and uses it to drive a simulated road network. Engineers can then evaluate how changes to infrastructure, traffic demand, or operating strategies could affect traffic conditions.
This connection between observation and simulation provides a foundation for testing what-if scenarios and comparing potential responses.

runs.text: Camera-informed simulation connects observed traffic with what-if analysis and engineering decisions.
A First Application in Signal Optimization
The initial application focuses on traffic signal timing at individual intersections and coordinated corridors.

Engineers can request an optimization through a conversational agent interface built with the VSS Blueprint. The platform evaluates candidate timing plans in simulation and returns a recommended plan, together with before-and-after measures such as delay and stops per vehicle. Results include a NEMA-format timing plan and a report for engineering review.
Demand estimates update every ten minutes, supporting repeated evaluation as traffic conditions change.
Results from Our Reference Deployment
We evaluated the pipeline using four recorded camera feeds from a busy downtown intersection, running on an
NVIDIA Brev
instance with two
NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs
In this deployment, the standard optimization workflow returned a plan in under two minutes. Recommended plans reduced
simulated control delay by 5–27%
c
ompared with the intersection’s existing timing plan.

These results demonstrate how camera-informed simulation can support traffic engineering decisions. The improvements were measured in simulation; field deployment requires engineering review and validation.
An Open Foundation for Urban Mobility
Built on TeraSim, originally developed at Mcity, University of Michigan, TeraSim
-DT
brings naturalistic traffic simulation to urban traffic operations.

Signal optimization is the first application. Our broader vision extends to evaluating traffic disruptions, planning for major events, and comparing transportation designs and management strategies. By exploring these possibilities in a digital twin, cities can better anticipate impacts and prepare their responses.
